newsitem.title: FRANCE: Giscard renews calls for weaker franc vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Giscard renews calls for weaker franc vs dollar.

text.p: Former French president Valery Giscard d'Estaing reiterated calls on Tuesday for a weaker franc and demanded a public debate about the level at which the unit should join the planned European single currency.

Giscard d'Estaing told French radio Europe 1 the currency should be trading at around 5.50 francs per dollar. It was at 5.16 francs to the dollar at 0955 GMT. He said his call for a weaker currency involved the relationship of the franc to the dollar, not the decade-old link between the franc and the mark.
"If we had a dollar worth 5.50 francs, the situation of most of our (economic) sectors would improve rapidly," he said.
Giscard renews calls for weaker franc vs dollar
He added that he had strong support from France's business community for his call for a weaker franc against the dollar.

Giscard d'Estaing's comments last week urging a weaker franc triggered a fall in the unit's value on international currency markets and brought condemnation by the government, which however said it did see room for the dollar to appreciate.
He reiterated he strongly supported monetary union but said an open debate about the level at which the franc joins monetary union, due to start on January 1, 1999 was vital.

"I hope there's a debate on the subject, that France and the government reflects and that when we decide what's in the best national interest, we act quickly," he said, and rounded on critics who attacked him for airing the issue.

"This is a problem which concerns all French people because it's linked to the economy's health and to unemployment," he said. The debate should not be conducted "clandestinely, in silence, in central banks," he said.
He reiterated his view that the franc should be fixed at a rate of seven francs per euro, the name of the new currency.
This would correspond to his suggested level of a dollar at 5.5 francs per dollar. This, however, would also correspond to 3.65 francs per mark, against 3.39 now.
Giscard d'Estaing insisted he was not calling for a depreciation of the franc against the mark but he said it was essential that monetary union benefit France.
"We're not a country whose decisions are taken by others, at least I hope not," he said. "This is a French problem, we do not want it to become a quarrel betweeen Germany and France."
He blamed inflexible French government economic policies for France's record 12.6 percent unemployment.
The policies, he said, "were condemning us to unemployment."
He said the government should follow the example of neighbouring countries, such as Britain and the Netherlands, and adopt a more flexible monetary policy to reduce jobless lines.

"We cannot let the French keep looking at unemployment at this level and tell them there's nothing we can do while our neighbours have improved their employment situation by using monetary policy," he said.
